title: Single-Family Starts Fall Amid Economic Uncertainty and Affordability Pressures
content: Overall housing starts decreased 2.8% in April to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.47 million units, according to a report from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and the U.S. Census Bureau.

title: Single-family housing starts fell in April, but multifamily gained momentum
content: April housing starts rose 4.6% year over year while single-family starts fell 2.4%, and new home inventory declined 4.6% from last year.

title: Why housing construction can’t grow at current demand levels
content: April housing starts ran at 1.465 million SAAR and single-family fell to 930,000 as completed new homes for sale held at 121,000.
